newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Liechtenstein ends 60-year old govt coalition.
newsitem.headline: Liechtenstein ends 60-year old govt coalition.

text.p: One of Liechtenstein's two major political parties voted on Monday to end what is thought to be the longest-serving government coalition in Europe.

At a political party congress, the Progressive Citizens Party Liechtenstein (FBPL) voted 368 to 31 to split from its coalition partner of nearly 60 years, the Fatherland Union (VU) party, Swiss news agency SDA reported.

The coalition has been in existence since 1938, the same year Hitler's Nazi regime annexed neighbouring Austria. Liechtenstein, a pocket-sized principality covering only 160 square km (62 square miles), is bordered by Switzerland and Austria.
In recent years, the FBPL has filled two seats in Liechtenstein's central governing body, with the other three seats filled by the VU.

The vote to split was expected after general elections on February 2, when the FBPL lost a parliamentary seat to the pro-ecology Free List party, giving the Free List a second seat at the FBPL's expense.
This left the FBPL with only 10 seats in Liechtenstein's 25-member parliament, while the VU maintained a clear majority with 13 seats.
Norbert Seeger, party president of the FBPL, told Reuters ahead of the vote that the move to create an opposition would allow the FBPL to gain a clearer profile.
"One will no longer be tied to government decisions. In this way the party will be freer. It (the decision to split) does not involve any single concrete issue," he said.
